t: They rolled over twice last night and pulled the blanket with them both times.
I woke before them and kept quiet until they stirred.
Their breathing tells me when they are truly asleep.
We should turn the bed away from that draft.
They warmed the cold side before I came home.
I heard them get up and pretended I was still asleep.
We keep waking each other and blaming the floorboards.
They were shivering, so I gave them more blanket without saying anything.
The bed feels too wide when they work late.
I should stop bringing muddy boots past the door. They have asked enough.
Their things have spread onto every shelf we own.
We need one more peg and one fewer argument about pegs.
They put my cup away where I never think to look.
I swept around their boots because moving them would start something.
We both avoid the loose stool and neither of us fixes it.
They want the window open. I want to keep feeling my hands.
I know which chores they did because the house feels easier afterwards.
We should wash the bedding before it starts standing by itself.
They left the last dry piece of wood for me.
The hearth burns longer when both of us remember it.
I should repair the latch before they remind me again.
They were right about moving the chest. I dislike how right they were.
We finally found a place for everything except the broom.
I like coming through the door and hearing them answer.
They can tell my mood by how I close the door.
I should leave work outside tonight and listen when they speak.
We argued over nothing this morning. I should end it before supper.
They laughed at my bad repair, then fixed it beside me.
I miss them most when the house is quiet enough to notice.
There is comfort in hearing somebody else bank the fire.
We have eaten from the same chipped bowls so often they feel matched.
They saved me a place near the fire without making a fuss.
I should bring home clean rushes before the floor smells damp.
We need to mend that blanket before one tear becomes two.
They always know when I have eaten elsewhere.
I promised a quiet evening. This time I should arrive before dark.
The roof makes its usual noise, and they still ask if it is safe.
I should thank them for making this place feel lived in.
Our house smells like smoke, damp wool, and whatever they cooked.
I know they are home because their coat is on my peg.
We keep saying we need another shelf. We keep doing nothing about it.
They sleep better after we talk, even when nothing gets settled.
I should not wait until bedtime to mention what is bothering me.
They make room for me even when they are angry.
We have learned which disagreements can wait until morning.
I should knock the mud from my boots before opening the door.
The door swings better since the hinge was tightened.
I still pause before entering, as if this might be somebody else's house.
The room holds heat better when I remember to shut the door.
That door moves whenever somebody passes. I should check the hinge.
I need to clear the doorway before somebody falls over that basket.
The latch catches unless I lift the door first.
A closed door makes the whole room quieter.
I should stop leaving firewood where the door strikes it.
Someone held the door for me today. I should return that kindness.
I turned over all night looking for a cooler patch.
The cold side of the bed was the only comfortable place.
I woke once, heard the walls creak, and went straight back to sleep.
The bedding needs airing after one more warm night.
I slept badly, but I slept under a roof.
A proper bed makes getting up harder than sleeping outside ever did.
I should shake the dust from the blanket before tonight.
The floor feels colder every morning. I need better rushes.
Smoke gathers near the rafters when the air is still.
I should scrape the soot before it falls into supper.
The smallest leak always lands where I want to sit.
I can hear the wind, but I cannot feel much of it.
This wall needs another coat before the weather turns.
The table rocks because one leg is shorter. A folded scrap will do.
I have swept the same corner three times and the dirt keeps winning.
There is room for another stool if I move the chest.
The shelf is crooked, but nothing has fallen yet.
I need a bowl near the door for wet things.
The house smells better after the window has been open awhile.
I should mend that gap before mice discover it.
Maybe belief is something people practice until it stops feeling borrowed.
I was ready to dismiss {god} yesterday. Today feels less simple.
Some answers arrive so late that I cannot tell whether they count.
I keep expecting certainty to arrive all at once. It never does.
The devout make faith look easy. They may simply hide the hard part.
I believe more when nobody is asking me to prove it.
A strange thing happened. Calling it divine still feels like another step.
I want {god} to be kind more than I want {god} to be real.
Yesterday I prayed without thinking. Today I noticed that I did.
Doubt is quieter after something good happens, but it never leaves.
I cannot tell whether gratitude is faith or simply good manners.
{god} may be listening. I should think before asking for anything.
One part of me expects an answer. The other prepares an explanation.
I have stopped mocking believers. That is not belief, but it is movement.
People keep asking what I believe as if I owe one answer forever.
I felt watched for a moment. It could have been nerves.
I nearly spoke a prayer aloud. Perhaps tomorrow I will.
The world looks ordinary today. I am not sure whether that disappoints me.
Belief comes easier near the shrine and fades by the time I reach work.
I can doubt the story and still hope it is true.
My left boot is wearing through faster than the right.
I should wash before somebody mentions the smell.
That cloud means rain, unless it means nothing again.
I have forgotten what I came over here to do.
The day started cold and somehow became too warm.
I should sit down before my legs decide for me.
Somebody has been sharpening tools nearby all morning.
I heard laughter and missed the reason for it.
There is always one job I remember after stopping.
My hands need washing and my clothes need worse.
I should drink some water before the headache starts.
The wind has changed. I can smell somebody's fire now.
I have walked this path enough to know every bad step.
That noise was probably nothing. Most noises are.
I need to trim my nails before one tears at work.
Supper sounds better than whatever I am doing now.
I should speak to somebody today instead of only nodding.
The village sounds different when everyone is working.
I have dirt in places dirt should not reach.
Tomorrow can have the task I keep avoiding today.
